{{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{infobox shinto shrine|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|神社|name=若一王子神社|image=[[File:Nyakuichiouji jinja-1.jpg|250px]]
若一王子神社 拝殿
（2018年7月22日撮影）|location=[[長野県]][[大町市]]大字[[大町 (大町市)|大町]]2097|ISO=JP-20|緯度度=36|緯度分=30|緯度秒=56.5|経度度=137|経度分=51|経度秒=12.5|ラベルcoordinates=|map=Japan Nagano|deity={{Ublist| 若一王子 | 天照大神 | 伊弉冉尊 | 仁品王 | 妹耶姫 }}|神体=|rank=県社・別表神社|established=（伝）[[垂仁天皇]]の時代（[[仁科濫觴記]]）|宮司=|main hall=[[春日造]]|alternative name={{Ublist| 若一の宮 | 王子権現 | [[若一王寺]] }}|札所等=|festival=[[7月17日]]|festival=}}'''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社|fr|Nyakuichi-jinja}} (若一王子神社, Nyakuichiōji jinja)''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in {{ill|10=ja|11=大町_(大町市)|Omachi}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=大町市|Ōmachi, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Ōmachi}}, [[Nagano Prefecture]] . Its former {{ill|10=ja|11=rank|rank}} was that of [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]], but it is currently [[Beppyo shrine|a beppyo shrine]] under [[Association of Shinto Shrines|the Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It worships {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} == Worshipped deities == The following five gods are enshrined here: * {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} – A god enshrined in the fifth shrine {{ill|10=ja|11=熊野那智大社|Kumano Nachi Taisha|en}} * [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Omikami]] * [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * {{ill|10=ja|11=仁品王|King Nishinao}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=妹耶姫|Princess Imoya}} [[ja:若一王子神社]] == history == '''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社}}''' is said to have originated during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], when Prince Nishina, who ruled the area, built a shrine dedicated to [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]], the goddess of water. {{Cite journal|last=三橋建 監修|date=2016-04|title=穂高神社・武水別神社 手長神社・若一王子神社|publisher=[[デアゴスティーニ・ジャパン]]|issue=115|page=14|和書}} The location where it was built was near a waterway called a "seki" (dam) that was developed by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科氏|the Nishina clan|de|Nishina_(Klan)}} during the Kamakura period, and was an important location for diverting water into the city center. {{Cite journal|last=太田勝一|last2=高橋康|title=長野県北西部、仁科山地の地質と斜面崩壊|url=https://www.omachi-sanpaku.com/sanpaku/bull/docs/bulletin8.pdf|journal=市立大町山岳博物館研究紀要|volume=8|pages=1-14|和書}} The temple was founded [[Kamakura period|in the Kamakura period]] when {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛遠|Nishina Morito}}, a local lord who ruled {{ill|10=ja|11=安曇郡|Azumi-gun|lt=the Azumi County}} area, made a pilgrimage to {{Ill|Kumano Gongen|simple|User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen|fr}} in [[Kii Province]] and invited {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji}}, who is enshrined in the fifth hall of Nachi Taisha, to be the guardian deity of {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科荘|Nishina Manor}} . {{Cite book|title=大町市史|publisher=|editor-last=|volume=|page=255|id=|和書}} Since then, the temple has been called "Nyakuichi no Miya" (Nyakuichioji Temple, Oji Gongen). During this time, Morito gained the favor of [[Emperor Go-Toba]] and served him as {{ill|10=ja|11=西面武士|a Western Guard warrior}} . When the Nishina clan was destroyed along with their lord the {{ill|7=Clan Takeda|10=ja|11=武田氏|Takeda clan|4=en|6=fr}}, the rulers of Japan after [[Oda Nobunaga]] made Azumi County the territory of successive lords of {{ill|10=ja|11=松本城|Matsumoto Castle|4=en}} and came under the protection of the Matsumoto Domain . During [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, when {{ill|10=ja|11=神仏分離|Shinbutsu bunri|lt=Shinto and Buddhism were separated|4=en|6=fr}}, the temple name was abolished and the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1931 ( [[Shōwa period|Showa]] 6), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in 1976 (Showa 51), it was added to the list of beppyo shrines of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Shinto-Buddhist syncretism == The shrine features both torii gates and shrine buildings, as seen in Shinto shrines, and Kannon halls and {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda|lt=three-storied pagodas}}, as seen in Buddhist temples, coexisting within the same precincts, preserving the appearance of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. It is said that the Nyakui Onji Shrine was preserved in this form because, during the Meiji Restoration, in response to the movement to abolish Buddhism initiated by the Matsumoto domain, the predecessors ingeniously built small embankments between each building, arguing that the shrine and the temple were separate entities. {{Cite book|title=若一王子神社昔語り|publisher=|year=2009|editor-last=大町の伝承文化を守る会|id=|和書}} . [[File:若一王子神社鳥居と三重塔.jpg|none|thumb| Torii gate and three-story pagoda of Nyakuiichioji Shrine]] {{Clear|right}} == Temple grounds == [[File:若一王子神社本殿.jpg|thumb|main hall]] [[File:若一王子神社観音堂.jpg|thumb| Kannon Hall (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|thumb| Three-story pagoda (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:若一王子神社のブナ.jpg|thumb| Beech trees growing within the temple grounds (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The main hall was built by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛康|Nishina Moriyasu}} in [[1556]] and is designated as an Important Cultural Property. The worship hall was donated to the temple in [[1975]] as part of the former shrine building of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] . The Kannon Hall to the east of the main hall houses a statue of the {{ill|10=ja|11=十一面観音|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Eleven-Headed Kannon|4=en}}, which is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakui. There is also a {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda}}. === building === The main buildings within the grounds are as follows: ; main hall (Important Cultural Property) : The one-bay shrine is made in the Kasuga style with wooden corners and a cypress bark roof. ; Kannon Hall (Nagano Prefectural Treasure) : Built in 1706 ( [[Hōei|Hoei]] 3). The building is three bays wide, has a hipped roof, thatched roof and a gabled entrance. A one-ken shingled roof is installed at the front. : A palace (shrine) is placed in the inner sanctuary. The palace is a one-bay, hip-and-gabled building with a gabled entrance and horizontal board roof. : There are carvings of celestial maidens on the handrails inside the veranda and a carving of a kirin on the front toad-legs. In the center of the outer sanctuary ceiling is a ink-painted dragon, and the inner sanctuary has a coffered ceiling with brightly colored flowers and birds painted between the coffers. : The Kannon Hall houses a bronze eleven-headed Kannon seated statue with its remains (Nagano Prefecture Treasure) and a wooden standing statue of the eleven-headed Kannon Bodhisattva (Omachi City Tangible Cultural Property). : The Nagano Prefectural Treasure, the bronze eleven-faced seated Kannon statue, is the principal image of the Kannon Hall and is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakuicho. The statue is 19 centimetres tall, and the panel has been removed, leaving only the Buddha body. On the other hand, the wooden standing statue of Eleven-Headed Kannon Bodhisattva is made of cypress wood and inlaid with wood, and parts of it were destroyed by fire. ; Three-story pagoda : It was built in 1711 (8th year of the Hoei era) with the support of Mokishoku Sankyo. It has three bays, three sides and a thatched roof. : On the lower floor, there are seated statues of the Five Wisdom Buddhas (Mahavairocana, Akshobhna, Treasures of Wisdom, Amitabha and Shaka Buddha). : Inside the toad-leg structure on the first floor are carved figures of the twelve Chinese zodiac animals with human bodies and animal faces. ; Other buildings : It houses a worship hall, a shrine office, Gokoku Shrine, and Yasaka Shrine. === Shrine forest === On April 30, 1965, {{Nowrap|17,186.4 [[平方メートル|m2]]}} was designated {{ill|10=ja|11=天然記念物|Natural monument|4=en}} by Nagano Prefecture. {{Cite web|title=若一王子神社社叢|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1615&seq=|access-date=2023-10-21|website=信州の文化財|publisher=八十二文化財団}} [[Chinju no Mori|The shrine grove]] is surrounded by coniferous trees, mainly cedars, but there are also scattered broadleaf trees and one {{ill|7=Hêtre du Japon|10=ja|11=ブナ|Fagus crenata|lt=beech tree|4=en|6=fr}} .{{Clear|right}} == festivals == [[File:若一王子神社由来.jpg|thumb| Origin of Nyakuichioji Shrine (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The festivals are as follows: === festival === * July 17 === annual celebration festival === * Fourth Sunday in July * Yabusame Ritual * Stage Events === Omachi Yabusame === (Source: {{Cite book|title=子ども達による大町流鏑馬|last=|publisher=大町流鏑馬保存会|year=2003|page=9-10|id=|和書}} ) * [[Yabusame|The Yabusame]] of Nyakuichioji Shrine, popularly known as Omachi Yabusame, is said to be one of the three major Yabusame in Japan, along with {{ill|10=ja|11=鶴岡八幡宮|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|4=en}} in Kamakura and [[Shimogamo Shrine|Kamo Shrine]] in Kyoto, and was brought to the area by the Nishina clan, who ruled the area for around 500 years from the Heian period through to the Kamakura period. It is said that this [[Jōkyū|tradition]] began in 829, when [[Emperor Go-Toba]] issues the order to pursue and kill {{ill|10=ja|11=北条義時|Hōjō Yoshitoki|4=en}}, and Nishina Morito offered a yabusame performance before the altar and prayed for good fortune in battle before setting out for battle. Nishina had a deep knowledge of Yabusame at Kamo Shrine, and is said to have brought it to his hometown of Omachi. * Until the Meiji Restoration, it was held jointly with {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科神明宮|Nishina Shinmei Shrine|4=en}} . The same archers performed the event at Nishina Shinmei Shrine on June 16th of the lunar calendar, and at Nyakuichioji Shrine the following day, the 17th, covering a distance of about two ri (approximately 2 ri), but after the Meiji Restoration, they began to hold the event separately. In Omachi, Shigeemon Ito of Kaminakacho proposed selecting archers from among the general parishioners, and donated horse equipment and costumes from his own pocket to each neighborhood, laying the foundation for the Omachi Yabusame, in which ten horsemen from ten neighborhoods compete as they do today. In 1971, it was designated a folk cultural property of Omachi City, and in 2001, it was designated by Nagano Prefecture. ( {{ill|10=ja|11=長野県指定文化財一覧|List of cultural properties designated by Nagano Prefecture|4=en}}) * A distinctive feature of Omachi Yabusame is that the archers are young boys between the ages of six and nine. The boy has makeup on his face, wears hunting clothes and a battle kimono, and is dressed as an archer, carrying a long sword and a Shigefuji bow, with arrows in his quiver. As a child of God possessed by God, I take great care to ensure that my feet do not touch the ground. The archers are called bobo by the locals, and the horses that the bobos ride are accompanied by mouthpieces, fan holders, hat holders, bodyguards, bow carriers, and attendants, all dressed in old-fashioned attire, and the sight of them parading around to the chant of "Hao, hao, hao" gives the performance the appearance of a feudal lord's procession. {{Clear|right}} == Cultural Assets == {{Col-begin}} {{Col-3}} '''Important Cultural Property (重要文化財)''' * Main Shrine (main hall) '''Nagano Prefecture Treasure (Nagano Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Property) (長野県宝（長野県指定有形文化財）)''' * {{ill|Three-Storied Pagoda|ja|三重塔}} * Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon, Remaining Part (十一面観音坐像御正体残闕) {{Col-3}} '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property (長野県指定無形民俗文化財)''' * Yabusame (Archery on horseback) (流鏑馬) '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Natural Monument (長野県指定天然記念物)''' * Shrine Grove (社叢) {{Col-3}} '''Omachi City Designated Tangible Cultural Property (大町市指定有形文化財)''' * Kannon Hall and its Repository (観音堂および厨子) * Standing Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon (十一面観音立像) * Former Portable Shrine of Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社の旧神輿) {{Col-end}} == Traffic access == * Approximately 10 minutes walk from {{ill|10=ja|11=北大町駅|Kita-Ōmachi Station|4=en}} on the [[East Japan Railway Company|JR]] {{ill|10=ja|11=大糸線|Ōito Line|4=en}} == Gallery == {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} – A god enshrined in the fifth shrine {{ill|10=ja|11=熊野那智大社|Kumano Nachi Taisha|en}} * [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Omikami]] * [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * {{ill|10=ja|11=仁品王|King Nishinao}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=妹耶姫|Princess Imoya}} [[ja:若一王子神社]] == history == '''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社}}''' is said to have originated during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], when Prince Nishina, who ruled the area, built a shrine dedicated to [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]], the goddess of water. {{Cite journal|last=三橋建 監修|date=2016-04|title=穂高神社・武水別神社 手長神社・若一王子神社|publisher=[[デアゴスティーニ・ジャパン]]|issue=115|page=14|和書}} The location where it was built was near a waterway called a "seki" (dam) that was developed by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科氏|the Nishina clan|de|Nishina_(Klan)}} during the Kamakura period, and was an important location for diverting water into the city center. {{Cite journal|last=太田勝一|last2=高橋康|title=長野県北西部、仁科山地の地質と斜面崩壊|url=https://www.omachi-sanpaku.com/sanpaku/bull/docs/bulletin8.pdf|journal=市立大町山岳博物館研究紀要|volume=8|pages=1-14|和書}} The temple was founded [[Kamakura period|in the Kamakura period]] when {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛遠|Nishina Morito}}, a local lord who ruled {{ill|10=ja|11=安曇郡|Azumi-gun|lt=the Azumi County}} area, made a pilgrimage to {{Ill|Kumano Gongen|simple|User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen|fr}} in [[Kii Province]] and invited {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji}}, who is enshrined in the fifth hall of Nachi Taisha, to be the guardian deity of {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科荘|Nishina Manor}} . {{Cite book|title=大町市史|publisher=|editor-last=|volume=|page=255|id=|和書}} Since then, the temple has been called "Nyakuichi no Miya" (Nyakuichioji Temple, Oji Gongen). During this time, Morito gained the favor of [[Emperor Go-Toba]] and served him as {{ill|10=ja|11=西面武士|a Western Guard warrior}} . When the Nishina clan was destroyed along with their lord the {{ill|7=Clan Takeda|10=ja|11=武田氏|Takeda clan|4=en|6=fr}}, the rulers of Japan after [[Oda Nobunaga]] made Azumi County the territory of successive lords of {{ill|10=ja|11=松本城|Matsumoto Castle|4=en}} and came under the protection of the Matsumoto Domain . During [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, when {{ill|10=ja|11=神仏分離|Shinbutsu bunri|lt=Shinto and Buddhism were separated|4=en|6=fr}}, the temple name was abolished and the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1931 ( [[Shōwa period|Showa]] 6), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in 1976 (Showa 51), it was added to the list of beppyo shrines of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Shinto-Buddhist syncretism == The shrine features both torii gates and shrine buildings, as seen in Shinto shrines, and Kannon halls and {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda|lt=three-storied pagodas}}, as seen in Buddhist temples, coexisting within the same precincts, preserving the appearance of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. It is said that the Nyakui Onji Shrine was preserved in this form because, during the Meiji Restoration, in response to the movement to abolish Buddhism initiated by the Matsumoto domain, the predecessors ingeniously built small embankments between each building, arguing that the shrine and the temple were separate entities. {{Cite book|title=若一王子神社昔語り|publisher=|year=2009|editor-last=大町の伝承文化を守る会|id=|和書}} . [[File:若一王子神社鳥居と三重塔.jpg|none|thumb| Torii gate and three-story pagoda of Nyakuiichioji Shrine]] {{Clear|right}} == Temple grounds == [[File:若一王子神社本殿.jpg|thumb|main hall]] [[File:若一王子神社観音堂.jpg|thumb| Kannon Hall (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|thumb| Three-story pagoda (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:若一王子神社のブナ.jpg|thumb| Beech trees growing within the temple grounds (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The main hall was built by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛康|Nishina Moriyasu}} in [[1556]] and is designated as an Important Cultural Property. The worship hall was donated to the temple in [[1975]] as part of the former shrine building of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] . The Kannon Hall to the east of the main hall houses a statue of the {{ill|10=ja|11=十一面観音|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Eleven-Headed Kannon|4=en}}, which is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakui. There is also a {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda}}. === building === The main buildings within the grounds are as follows: ; main hall (Important Cultural Property) : The one-bay shrine is made in the Kasuga style with wooden corners and a cypress bark roof. ; Kannon Hall (Nagano Prefectural Treasure) : Built in 1706 ( [[Hōei|Hoei]] 3). The building is three bays wide, has a hipped roof, thatched roof and a gabled entrance. A one-ken shingled roof is installed at the front. : A palace (shrine) is placed in the inner sanctuary. The palace is a one-bay, hip-and-gabled building with a gabled entrance and horizontal board roof. : There are carvings of celestial maidens on the handrails inside the veranda and a carving of a kirin on the front toad-legs. In the center of the outer sanctuary ceiling is a ink-painted dragon, and the inner sanctuary has a coffered ceiling with brightly colored flowers and birds painted between the coffers. : The Kannon Hall houses a bronze eleven-headed Kannon seated statue with its remains (Nagano Prefecture Treasure) and a wooden standing statue of the eleven-headed Kannon Bodhisattva (Omachi City Tangible Cultural Property). : The Nagano Prefectural Treasure, the bronze eleven-faced seated Kannon statue, is the principal image of the Kannon Hall and is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakuicho. The statue is 19 centimetres tall, and the panel has been removed, leaving only the Buddha body. On the other hand, the wooden standing statue of Eleven-Headed Kannon Bodhisattva is made of cypress wood and inlaid with wood, and parts of it were destroyed by fire. ; Three-story pagoda : It was built in 1711 (8th year of the Hoei era) with the support of Mokishoku Sankyo. It has three bays, three sides and a thatched roof. : On the lower floor, there are seated statues of the Five Wisdom Buddhas (Mahavairocana, Akshobhna, Treasures of Wisdom, Amitabha and Shaka Buddha). : Inside the toad-leg structure on the first floor are carved figures of the twelve Chinese zodiac animals with human bodies and animal faces. ; Other buildings : It houses a worship hall, a shrine office, Gokoku Shrine, and Yasaka Shrine. === Shrine forest === On April 30, 1965, {{Nowrap|17,186.4 [[平方メートル|m2]]}} was designated {{ill|10=ja|11=天然記念物|Natural monument|4=en}} by Nagano Prefecture. {{Cite web|title=若一王子神社社叢|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1615&seq=|access-date=2023-10-21|website=信州の文化財|publisher=八十二文化財団}} [[Chinju no Mori|The shrine grove]] is surrounded by coniferous trees, mainly cedars, but there are also scattered broadleaf trees and one {{ill|7=Hêtre du Japon|10=ja|11=ブナ|Fagus crenata|lt=beech tree|4=en|6=fr}} .{{Clear|right}} == festivals == [[File:若一王子神社由来.jpg|thumb| Origin of Nyakuichioji Shrine (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The festivals are as follows: === festival === * July 17 === annual celebration festival === * Fourth Sunday in July * Yabusame Ritual * Stage Events === Omachi Yabusame === (Source: {{Cite book|title=子ども達による大町流鏑馬|last=|publisher=大町流鏑馬保存会|year=2003|page=9-10|id=|和書}} ) * [[Yabusame|The Yabusame]] of Nyakuichioji Shrine, popularly known as Omachi Yabusame, is said to be one of the three major Yabusame in Japan, along with {{ill|10=ja|11=鶴岡八幡宮|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|4=en}} in Kamakura and [[Shimogamo Shrine|Kamo Shrine]] in Kyoto, and was brought to the area by the Nishina clan, who ruled the area for around 500 years from the Heian period through to the Kamakura period. It is said that this [[Jōkyū|tradition]] began in 829, when [[Emperor Go-Toba]] issues the order to pursue and kill {{ill|10=ja|11=北条義時|Hōjō Yoshitoki|4=en}}, and Nishina Morito offered a yabusame performance before the altar and prayed for good fortune in battle before setting out for battle. Nishina had a deep knowledge of Yabusame at Kamo Shrine, and is said to have brought it to his hometown of Omachi. * Until the Meiji Restoration, it was held jointly with {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科神明宮|Nishina Shinmei Shrine|4=en}} . The same archers performed the event at Nishina Shinmei Shrine on June 16th of the lunar calendar, and at Nyakuichioji Shrine the following day, the 17th, covering a distance of about two ri (approximately 2 ri), but after the Meiji Restoration, they began to hold the event separately. In Omachi, Shigeemon Ito of Kaminakacho proposed selecting archers from among the general parishioners, and donated horse equipment and costumes from his own pocket to each neighborhood, laying the foundation for the Omachi Yabusame, in which ten horsemen from ten neighborhoods compete as they do today. In 1971, it was designated a folk cultural property of Omachi City, and in 2001, it was designated by Nagano Prefecture. ( {{ill|10=ja|11=長野県指定文化財一覧|List of cultural properties designated by Nagano Prefecture|4=en}}) * A distinctive feature of Omachi Yabusame is that the archers are young boys between the ages of six and nine. The boy has makeup on his face, wears hunting clothes and a battle kimono, and is dressed as an archer, carrying a long sword and a Shigefuji bow, with arrows in his quiver. As a child of God possessed by God, I take great care to ensure that my feet do not touch the ground. The archers are called bobo by the locals, and the horses that the bobos ride are accompanied by mouthpieces, fan holders, hat holders, bodyguards, bow carriers, and attendants, all dressed in old-fashioned attire, and the sight of them parading around to the chant of "Hao, hao, hao" gives the performance the appearance of a feudal lord's procession. {{Clear|right}} == Cultural Assets == {{Col-begin}} {{Col-3}} '''Important Cultural Property (重要文化財)''' * Main Shrine (main hall) '''Nagano Prefecture Treasure (Nagano Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Property) (長野県宝（長野県指定有形文化財）)''' * {{ill|Three-Storied Pagoda|ja|三重塔}} * Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon, Remaining Part (十一面観音坐像御正体残闕) {{Col-3}} '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property (長野県指定無形民俗文化財)''' * Yabusame (Archery on horseback) (流鏑馬) '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Natural Monument (長野県指定天然記念物)''' * Shrine Grove (社叢) {{Col-3}} '''Omachi City Designated Tangible Cultural Property (大町市指定有形文化財)''' * Kannon Hall and its Repository (観音堂および厨子) * Standing Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon (十一面観音立像) * Former Portable Shrine of Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社の旧神輿) {{Col-end}} == Traffic access == * Approximately 10 minutes walk from {{ill|10=ja|11=北大町駅|Kita-Ōmachi Station|4=en}} on the [[East Japan Railway Company|JR]] {{ill|10=ja|11=大糸線|Ōito Line|4=en}} == Gallery == There is also a {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda}}. === building === The main buildings within the grounds are as follows: ; main hall (Important Cultural Property) : The one-bay shrine is made in the Kasuga style with wooden corners and a cypress bark roof. ; Kannon Hall (Nagano Prefectural Treasure) : Built in 1706 ( [[Hōei|Hoei]] 3). The building is three bays wide, has a hipped roof, thatched roof and a gabled entrance. A one-ken shingled roof is installed at the front. : A palace (shrine) is placed in the inner sanctuary. The palace is a one-bay, hip-and-gabled building with a gabled entrance and horizontal board roof. : There are carvings of celestial maidens on the handrails inside the veranda and a carving of a kirin on the front toad-legs. In the center of the outer sanctuary ceiling is a ink-painted dragon, and the inner sanctuary has a coffered ceiling with brightly colored flowers and birds painted between the coffers. : The Kannon Hall houses a bronze eleven-headed Kannon seated statue with its remains (Nagano Prefecture Treasure) and a wooden standing statue of the eleven-headed Kannon Bodhisattva (Omachi City Tangible Cultural Property). : The Nagano Prefectural Treasure, the bronze eleven-faced seated Kannon statue, is the principal image of the Kannon Hall and is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakuicho. The statue is 19 centimetres tall, and the panel has been removed, leaving only the Buddha body. On the other hand, the wooden standing statue of Eleven-Headed Kannon Bodhisattva is made of cypress wood and inlaid with wood, and parts of it were destroyed by fire. ; Three-story pagoda : It was built in 1711 (8th year of the Hoei era) with the support of Mokishoku Sankyo. It has three bays, three sides and a thatched roof. : On the lower floor, there are seated statues of the Five Wisdom Buddhas (Mahavairocana, Akshobhna, Treasures of Wisdom, Amitabha and Shaka Buddha). : Inside the toad-leg structure on the first floor are carved figures of the twelve Chinese zodiac animals with human bodies and animal faces. ; Other buildings : It houses a worship hall, a shrine office, Gokoku Shrine, and Yasaka Shrine. === Shrine forest === On April 30, 1965, {{Nowrap|17,186.4 [[平方メートル|m2]]}} was designated {{ill|10=ja|11=天然記念物|Natural monument|4=en}} by Nagano Prefecture. {{Cite web|title=若一王子神社社叢|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1615&seq=|access-date=2023-10-21|website=信州の文化財|publisher=八十二文化財団}} [[Chinju no Mori|The shrine grove]] is surrounded by coniferous trees, mainly cedars, but there are also scattered broadleaf trees and one {{ill|7=Hêtre du Japon|10=ja|11=ブナ|Fagus crenata|lt=beech tree|4=en|6=fr}} .{{Clear|right}} == festivals == [[File:若一王子神社由来.jpg|thumb| Origin of Nyakuichioji Shrine (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The festivals are as follows: === festival === * July 17 === annual celebration festival === * Fourth Sunday in July * Yabusame Ritual * Stage Events === Omachi Yabusame === (Source: {{Cite book|title=子ども達による大町流鏑馬|last=|publisher=大町流鏑馬保存会|year=2003|page=9-10|id=|和書}} ) * [[Yabusame|The Yabusame]] of Nyakuichioji Shrine, popularly known as Omachi Yabusame, is said to be one of the three major Yabusame in Japan, along with {{ill|10=ja|11=鶴岡八幡宮|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|4=en}} in Kamakura and [[Shimogamo Shrine|Kamo Shrine]] in Kyoto, and was brought to the area by the Nishina clan, who ruled the area for around 500 years from the Heian period through to the Kamakura period. It is said that this [[Jōkyū|tradition]] began in 829, when [[Emperor Go-Toba]] issues the order to pursue and kill {{ill|10=ja|11=北条義時|Hōjō Yoshitoki|4=en}}, and Nishina Morito offered a yabusame performance before the altar and prayed for good fortune in battle before setting out for battle. The same archers performed the event at Nishina Shinmei Shrine on June 16th of the lunar calendar, and at Nyakuichioji Shrine the following day, the 17th, covering a distance of about two ri (approximately 2 ri), but after the Meiji Restoration, they began to hold the event separately. In Omachi, Shigeemon Ito of Kaminakacho proposed selecting archers from among the general parishioners, and donated horse equipment and costumes from his own pocket to each neighborhood, laying the foundation for the Omachi Yabusame, in which ten horsemen from ten neighborhoods compete as they do today. In 1971, it was designated a folk cultural property of Omachi City, and in 2001, it was designated by Nagano Prefecture. ( {{ill|10=ja|11=長野県指定文化財一覧|List of cultural properties designated by Nagano Prefecture|4=en}}) * A distinctive feature of Omachi Yabusame is that the archers are young boys between the ages of six and nine. The boy has makeup on his face, wears hunting clothes and a battle kimono, and is dressed as an archer, carrying a long sword and a Shigefuji bow, with arrows in his quiver. As a child of God possessed by God, I take great care to ensure that my feet do not touch the ground. The archers are called bobo by the locals, and the horses that the bobos ride are accompanied by mouthpieces, fan holders, hat holders, bodyguards, bow carriers, and attendants, all dressed in old-fashioned attire, and the sight of them parading around to the chant of "Hao, hao, hao" gives the performance the appearance of a feudal lord's procession. {{Clear|right}} == Cultural Assets == 若一王子神社 拝殿
（2018年7月22日撮影）|location=[[長野県]][[大町市]]大字[[大町 (大町市)|大町]]2097|ISO=JP-20|緯度度=36|緯度分=30|緯度秒=56.5|経度度=137|経度分=51|経度秒=12.5|ラベルcoordinates=|map=Japan Nagano|deity={{Ublist| 若一王子 | 天照大神 | 伊弉冉尊 | 仁品王 | 妹耶姫 }}|神体=|rank=県社・別表神社|established=（伝）[[垂仁天皇]]の時代（[[仁科濫觴記]]）|宮司=|main hall=[[春日造]]|alternative name={{Ublist| 若一の宮 | 王子権現 | [[若一王寺]] }}|札所等=|festival=[[7月17日]]|festival=}}'''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社|fr|Nyakuichi-jinja}} (若一王子神社, Nyakuichiōji jinja)''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in {{ill|10=ja|11=大町_(大町市)|Omachi}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=大町市|Ōmachi, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Ōmachi}}, [[Nagano Prefecture]] . Its former {{ill|10=ja|11=rank|rank}} was that of [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]], but it is currently [[Beppyo shrine|a beppyo shrine]] under [[Association of Shinto Shrines|the Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It worships {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} == Worshipped deities == The following five gods are enshrined here: * {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} – A god enshrined in the fifth shrine {{ill|10=ja|11=熊野那智大社|Kumano Nachi Taisha|en}} * [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Omikami]] * [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * {{ill|10=ja|11=仁品王|King Nishinao}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=妹耶姫|Princess Imoya}} [[ja:若一王子神社]] == history == '''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社}}''' is said to have originated during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], when Prince Nishina, who ruled the area, built a shrine dedicated to [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]], the goddess of water. {{Cite journal|last=三橋建 監修|date=2016-04|title=穂高神社・武水別神社 手長神社・若一王子神社|publisher=[[デアゴスティーニ・ジャパン]]|issue=115|page=14|和書}} The location where it was built was near a waterway called a "seki" (dam) that was developed by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科氏|the Nishina clan|de|Nishina_(Klan)}} during the Kamakura period, and was an important location for diverting water into the city center. {{Cite journal|last=太田勝一|last2=高橋康|title=長野県北西部、仁科山地の地質と斜面崩壊|url=https://www.omachi-sanpaku.com/sanpaku/bull/docs/bulletin8.pdf|journal=市立大町山岳博物館研究紀要|volume=8|pages=1-14|和書}} The temple was founded [[Kamakura period|in the Kamakura period]] when {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛遠|Nishina Morito}}, a local lord who ruled {{ill|10=ja|11=安曇郡|Azumi-gun|lt=the Azumi County}} area, made a pilgrimage to {{Ill|Kumano Gongen|simple|User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen|fr}} in [[Kii Province]] and invited {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji}}, who is enshrined in the fifth hall of Nachi Taisha, to be the guardian deity of {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科荘|Nishina Manor}} . {{Cite book|title=大町市史|publisher=|editor-last=|volume=|page=255|id=|和書}} Since then, the temple has been called "Nyakuichi no Miya" (Nyakuichioji Temple, Oji Gongen). During this time, Morito gained the favor of [[Emperor Go-Toba]] and served him as {{ill|10=ja|11=西面武士|a Western Guard warrior}} . When the Nishina clan was destroyed along with their lord the {{ill|7=Clan Takeda|10=ja|11=武田氏|Takeda clan|4=en|6=fr}}, the rulers of Japan after [[Oda Nobunaga]] made Azumi County the territory of successive lords of {{ill|10=ja|11=松本城|Matsumoto Castle|4=en}} and came under the protection of the Matsumoto Domain . During [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, when {{ill|10=ja|11=神仏分離|Shinbutsu bunri|lt=Shinto and Buddhism were separated|4=en|6=fr}}, the temple name was abolished and the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1931 ( [[Shōwa period|Showa]] 6), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in 1976 (Showa 51), it was added to the list of beppyo shrines of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Shinto-Buddhist syncretism == The shrine features both torii gates and shrine buildings, as seen in Shinto shrines, and Kannon halls and {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda|lt=three-storied pagodas}}, as seen in Buddhist temples, coexisting within the same precincts, preserving the appearance of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. It is said that the Nyakui Onji Shrine was preserved in this form because, during the Meiji Restoration, in response to the movement to abolish Buddhism initiated by the Matsumoto domain, the predecessors ingeniously built small embankments between each building, arguing that the shrine and the temple were separate entities. {{Cite book|title=若一王子神社昔語り|publisher=|year=2009|editor-last=大町の伝承文化を守る会|id=|和書}} . {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{infobox shinto shrine|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|神社|name=若一王子神社|image=[[File:Nyakuichiouji jinja-1.jpg|250px]]
若一王子神社 拝殿
（2018年7月22日撮影）|location=[[長野県]][[大町市]]大字[[大町 (大町市)|大町]]2097|ISO=JP-20|緯度度=36|緯度分=30|緯度秒=56.5|経度度=137|経度分=51|経度秒=12.5|ラベルcoordinates=|map=Japan Nagano|deity={{Ublist| 若一王子 | 天照大神 | 伊弉冉尊 | 仁品王 | 妹耶姫 }}|神体=|rank=県社・別表神社|established=（伝）[[垂仁天皇]]の時代（[[仁科濫觴記]]）|宮司=|main hall=[[春日造]]|alternative name={{Ublist| 若一の宮 | 王子権現 | [[若一王寺]] }}|札所等=|festival=[[7月17日]]|festival=}}'''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社|fr|Nyakuichi-jinja}} (若一王子神社, Nyakuichiōji jinja)''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in {{ill|10=ja|11=大町_(大町市)|Omachi}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=大町市|Ōmachi, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Ōmachi}}, [[Nagano Prefecture]] . Its former {{ill|10=ja|11=rank|rank}} was that of [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]], but it is currently [[Beppyo shrine|a beppyo shrine]] under [[Association of Shinto Shrines|the Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It worships {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} == Worshipped deities == The following five gods are enshrined here: * {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} – A god enshrined in the fifth shrine {{ill|10=ja|11=熊野那智大社|Kumano Nachi Taisha|en}} * [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Omikami]] * [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * {{ill|10=ja|11=仁品王|King Nishinao}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=妹耶姫|Princess Imoya}} [[ja:若一王子神社]] == history == '''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社}}''' is said to have originated during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], when Prince Nishina, who ruled the area, built a shrine dedicated to [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]], the goddess of water. {{Cite journal|last=三橋建 監修|date=2016-04|title=穂高神社・武水別神社 手長神社・若一王子神社|publisher=[[デアゴスティーニ・ジャパン]]|issue=115|page=14|和書}} The location where it was built was near a waterway called a "seki" (dam) that was developed by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科氏|the Nishina clan|de|Nishina_(Klan)}} during the Kamakura period, and was an important location for diverting water into the city center. {{Cite journal|last=太田勝一|last2=高橋康|title=長野県北西部、仁科山地の地質と斜面崩壊|url=https://www.omachi-sanpaku.com/sanpaku/bull/docs/bulletin8.pdf|journal=市立大町山岳博物館研究紀要|volume=8|pages=1-14|和書}} The temple was founded [[Kamakura period|in the Kamakura period]] when {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛遠|Nishina Morito}}, a local lord who ruled {{ill|10=ja|11=安曇郡|Azumi-gun|lt=the Azumi County}} area, made a pilgrimage to {{Ill|Kumano Gongen|simple|User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen|fr}} in [[Kii Province]] and invited {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji}}, who is enshrined in the fifth hall of Nachi Taisha, to be the guardian deity of {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科荘|Nishina Manor}} . {{Cite book|title=大町市史|publisher=|editor-last=|volume=|page=255|id=|和書}} Since then, the temple has been called "Nyakuichi no Miya" (Nyakuichioji Temple, Oji Gongen). During this time, Morito gained the favor of [[Emperor Go-Toba]] and served him as {{ill|10=ja|11=西面武士|a Western Guard warrior}} . When the Nishina clan was destroyed along with their lord the {{ill|7=Clan Takeda|10=ja|11=武田氏|Takeda clan|4=en|6=fr}}, the rulers of Japan after [[Oda Nobunaga]] made Azumi County the territory of successive lords of {{ill|10=ja|11=松本城|Matsumoto Castle|4=en}} and came under the protection of the Matsumoto Domain . During [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, when {{ill|10=ja|11=神仏分離|Shinbutsu bunri|lt=Shinto and Buddhism were separated|4=en|6=fr}}, the temple name was abolished and the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1931 ( [[Shōwa period|Showa]] 6), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in 1976 (Showa 51), it was added to the list of beppyo shrines of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Shinto-Buddhist syncretism == The shrine features both torii gates and shrine buildings, as seen in Shinto shrines, and Kannon halls and {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda|lt=three-storied pagodas}}, as seen in Buddhist temples, coexisting within the same precincts, preserving the appearance of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. It is said that the Nyakui Onji Shrine was preserved in this form because, during the Meiji Restoration, in response to the movement to abolish Buddhism initiated by the Matsumoto domain, the predecessors ingeniously built small embankments between each building, arguing that the shrine and the temple were separate entities. {{Cite book|title=若一王子神社昔語り|publisher=|year=2009|editor-last=大町の伝承文化を守る会|id=|和書}} . [[File:若一王子神社鳥居と三重塔.jpg|none|thumb| Torii gate and three-story pagoda of Nyakuiichioji Shrine]] {{Clear|right}} == Temple grounds == [[File:若一王子神社本殿.jpg|thumb|main hall]] [[File:若一王子神社観音堂.jpg|thumb| Kannon Hall (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|thumb| Three-story pagoda (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:若一王子神社のブナ.jpg|thumb| Beech trees growing within the temple grounds (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The main hall was built by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛康|Nishina Moriyasu}} in [[1556]] and is designated as an Important Cultural Property. The worship hall was donated to the temple in [[1975]] as part of the former shrine building of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] . The Kannon Hall to the east of the main hall houses a statue of the {{ill|10=ja|11=十一面観音|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Eleven-Headed Kannon|4=en}}, which is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakui. There is also a {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda}}. === building === The main buildings within the grounds are as follows: ; main hall (Important Cultural Property) : The one-bay shrine is made in the Kasuga style with wooden corners and a cypress bark roof. ; Kannon Hall (Nagano Prefectural Treasure) : Built in 1706 ( [[Hōei|Hoei]] 3). The building is three bays wide, has a hipped roof, thatched roof and a gabled entrance. A one-ken shingled roof is installed at the front. : A palace (shrine) is placed in the inner sanctuary. The palace is a one-bay, hip-and-gabled building with a gabled entrance and horizontal board roof. : There are carvings of celestial maidens on the handrails inside the veranda and a carving of a kirin on the front toad-legs. In the center of the outer sanctuary ceiling is a ink-painted dragon, and the inner sanctuary has a coffered ceiling with brightly colored flowers and birds painted between the coffers. : The Kannon Hall houses a bronze eleven-headed Kannon seated statue with its remains (Nagano Prefecture Treasure) and a wooden standing statue of the eleven-headed Kannon Bodhisattva (Omachi City Tangible Cultural Property). : The Nagano Prefectural Treasure, the bronze eleven-faced seated Kannon statue, is the principal image of the Kannon Hall and is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakuicho. The statue is 19 centimetres tall, and the panel has been removed, leaving only the Buddha body. On the other hand, the wooden standing statue of Eleven-Headed Kannon Bodhisattva is made of cypress wood and inlaid with wood, and parts of it were destroyed by fire. ; Three-story pagoda : It was built in 1711 (8th year of the Hoei era) with the support of Mokishoku Sankyo. It has three bays, three sides and a thatched roof. : On the lower floor, there are seated statues of the Five Wisdom Buddhas (Mahavairocana, Akshobhna, Treasures of Wisdom, Amitabha and Shaka Buddha). : Inside the toad-leg structure on the first floor are carved figures of the twelve Chinese zodiac animals with human bodies and animal faces. ; Other buildings : It houses a worship hall, a shrine office, Gokoku Shrine, and Yasaka Shrine. === Shrine forest === On April 30, 1965, {{Nowrap|17,186.4 [[平方メートル|m2]]}} was designated {{ill|10=ja|11=天然記念物|Natural monument|4=en}} by Nagano Prefecture. {{Cite web|title=若一王子神社社叢|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1615&seq=|access-date=2023-10-21|website=信州の文化財|publisher=八十二文化財団}} [[Chinju no Mori|The shrine grove]] is surrounded by coniferous trees, mainly cedars, but there are also scattered broadleaf trees and one {{ill|7=Hêtre du Japon|10=ja|11=ブナ|Fagus crenata|lt=beech tree|4=en|6=fr}} .{{Clear|right}} == festivals == [[File:若一王子神社由来.jpg|thumb| Origin of Nyakuichioji Shrine (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The festivals are as follows: === festival === * July 17 === annual celebration festival === * Fourth Sunday in July * Yabusame Ritual * Stage Events === Omachi Yabusame === (Source: {{Cite book|title=子ども達による大町流鏑馬|last=|publisher=大町流鏑馬保存会|year=2003|page=9-10|id=|和書}} ) * [[Yabusame|The Yabusame]] of Nyakuichioji Shrine, popularly known as Omachi Yabusame, is said to be one of the three major Yabusame in Japan, along with {{ill|10=ja|11=鶴岡八幡宮|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|4=en}} in Kamakura and [[Shimogamo Shrine|Kamo Shrine]] in Kyoto, and was brought to the area by the Nishina clan, who ruled the area for around 500 years from the Heian period through to the Kamakura period. It is said that this [[Jōkyū|tradition]] began in 829, when [[Emperor Go-Toba]] issues the order to pursue and kill {{ill|10=ja|11=北条義時|Hōjō Yoshitoki|4=en}}, and Nishina Morito offered a yabusame performance before the altar and prayed for good fortune in battle before setting out for battle. Nishina had a deep knowledge of Yabusame at Kamo Shrine, and is said to have brought it to his hometown of Omachi. * Until the Meiji Restoration, it was held jointly with {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科神明宮|Nishina Shinmei Shrine|4=en}} . The same archers performed the event at Nishina Shinmei Shrine on June 16th of the lunar calendar, and at Nyakuichioji Shrine the following day, the 17th, covering a distance of about two ri (approximately 2 ri), but after the Meiji Restoration, they began to hold the event separately. In Omachi, Shigeemon Ito of Kaminakacho proposed selecting archers from among the general parishioners, and donated horse equipment and costumes from his own pocket to each neighborhood, laying the foundation for the Omachi Yabusame, in which ten horsemen from ten neighborhoods compete as they do today. In 1971, it was designated a folk cultural property of Omachi City, and in 2001, it was designated by Nagano Prefecture. ( {{ill|10=ja|11=長野県指定文化財一覧|List of cultural properties designated by Nagano Prefecture|4=en}}) * A distinctive feature of Omachi Yabusame is that the archers are young boys between the ages of six and nine. The boy has makeup on his face, wears hunting clothes and a battle kimono, and is dressed as an archer, carrying a long sword and a Shigefuji bow, with arrows in his quiver. As a child of God possessed by God, I take great care to ensure that my feet do not touch the ground. The archers are called bobo by the locals, and the horses that the bobos ride are accompanied by mouthpieces, fan holders, hat holders, bodyguards, bow carriers, and attendants, all dressed in old-fashioned attire, and the sight of them parading around to the chant of "Hao, hao, hao" gives the performance the appearance of a feudal lord's procession. {{Clear|right}} == Cultural Assets == {{User:Immanuelle/Promising Draft}} {{infobox shinto shrine|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|神社|name=若一王子神社|image=[[File:Nyakuichiouji jinja-1.jpg|250px]]
若一王子神社 拝殿
（2018年7月22日撮影）|location=[[長野県]][[大町市]]大字[[大町 (大町市)|大町]]2097|ISO=JP-20|緯度度=36|緯度分=30|緯度秒=56.5|経度度=137|経度分=51|経度秒=12.5|ラベルcoordinates=|map=Japan Nagano|deity={{Ublist| 若一王子 | 天照大神 | 伊弉冉尊 | 仁品王 | 妹耶姫 }}|神体=|rank=県社・別表神社|established=（伝）[[垂仁天皇]]の時代（[[仁科濫觴記]]）|宮司=|main hall=[[春日造]]|alternative name={{Ublist| 若一の宮 | 王子権現 | [[若一王寺]] }}|札所等=|festival=[[7月17日]]|festival=}}'''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社|fr|Nyakuichi-jinja}} (若一王子神社, Nyakuichiōji jinja)''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in {{ill|10=ja|11=大町_(大町市)|Omachi}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=大町市|Ōmachi, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Ōmachi}}, [[Nagano Prefecture]] . Its former {{ill|10=ja|11=rank|rank}} was that of [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]], but it is currently [[Beppyo shrine|a beppyo shrine]] under [[Association of Shinto Shrines|the Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It worships {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} == Worshipped deities == The following five gods are enshrined here: * {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} – A god enshrined in the fifth shrine {{ill|10=ja|11=熊野那智大社|Kumano Nachi Taisha|en}} * [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Omikami]] * [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * {{ill|10=ja|11=仁品王|King Nishinao}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=妹耶姫|Princess Imoya}} [[ja:若一王子神社]] == history == '''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社}}''' is said to have originated during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], when Prince Nishina, who ruled the area, built a shrine dedicated to [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]], the goddess of water. {{Cite journal|last=三橋建 監修|date=2016-04|title=穂高神社・武水別神社 手長神社・若一王子神社|publisher=[[デアゴスティーニ・ジャパン]]|issue=115|page=14|和書}} The location where it was built was near a waterway called a "seki" (dam) that was developed by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科氏|the Nishina clan|de|Nishina_(Klan)}} during the Kamakura period, and was an important location for diverting water into the city center. {{Cite journal|last=太田勝一|last2=高橋康|title=長野県北西部、仁科山地の地質と斜面崩壊|url=https://www.omachi-sanpaku.com/sanpaku/bull/docs/bulletin8.pdf|journal=市立大町山岳博物館研究紀要|volume=8|pages=1-14|和書}} The temple was founded [[Kamakura period|in the Kamakura period]] when {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛遠|Nishina Morito}}, a local lord who ruled {{ill|10=ja|11=安曇郡|Azumi-gun|lt=the Azumi County}} area, made a pilgrimage to {{Ill|Kumano Gongen|simple|User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen|fr}} in [[Kii Province]] and invited {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji}}, who is enshrined in the fifth hall of Nachi Taisha, to be the guardian deity of {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科荘|Nishina Manor}} . {{Cite book|title=大町市史|publisher=|editor-last=|volume=|page=255|id=|和書}} Since then, the temple has been called "Nyakuichi no Miya" (Nyakuichioji Temple, Oji Gongen). During this time, Morito gained the favor of [[Emperor Go-Toba]] and served him as {{ill|10=ja|11=西面武士|a Western Guard warrior}} . When the Nishina clan was destroyed along with their lord the {{ill|7=Clan Takeda|10=ja|11=武田氏|Takeda clan|4=en|6=fr}}, the rulers of Japan after [[Oda Nobunaga]] made Azumi County the territory of successive lords of {{ill|10=ja|11=松本城|Matsumoto Castle|4=en}} and came under the protection of the Matsumoto Domain . During [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, when {{ill|10=ja|11=神仏分離|Shinbutsu bunri|lt=Shinto and Buddhism were separated|4=en|6=fr}}, the temple name was abolished and the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1931 ( [[Shōwa period|Showa]] 6), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in 1976 (Showa 51), it was added to the list of beppyo shrines of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Shinto-Buddhist syncretism == The shrine features both torii gates and shrine buildings, as seen in Shinto shrines, and Kannon halls and {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda|lt=three-storied pagodas}}, as seen in Buddhist temples, coexisting within the same precincts, preserving the appearance of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. It is said that the Nyakui Onji Shrine was preserved in this form because, during the Meiji Restoration, in response to the movement to abolish Buddhism initiated by the Matsumoto domain, the predecessors ingeniously built small embankments between each building, arguing that the shrine and the temple were separate entities. {{Cite book|title=若一王子神社昔語り|publisher=|year=2009|editor-last=大町の伝承文化を守る会|id=|和書}} . [[File:若一王子神社鳥居と三重塔.jpg|none|thumb| Torii gate and three-story pagoda of Nyakuiichioji Shrine]] {{Clear|right}} == Temple grounds == [[File:若一王子神社本殿.jpg|thumb|main hall]] [[File:若一王子神社観音堂.jpg|thumb| Kannon Hall (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|thumb| Three-story pagoda (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:若一王子神社のブナ.jpg|thumb| Beech trees growing within the temple grounds (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The main hall was built by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛康|Nishina Moriyasu}} in [[1556]] and is designated as an Important Cultural Property. The worship hall was donated to the temple in [[1975]] as part of the former shrine building of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] . The Kannon Hall to the east of the main hall houses a statue of the {{ill|10=ja|11=十一面観音|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Eleven-Headed Kannon|4=en}}, which is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakui. There is also a {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda}}. === building === The main buildings within the grounds are as follows: ; main hall (Important Cultural Property) : The one-bay shrine is made in the Kasuga style with wooden corners and a cypress bark roof. ; Kannon Hall (Nagano Prefectural Treasure) : Built in 1706 ( [[Hōei|Hoei]] 3). The building is three bays wide, has a hipped roof, thatched roof and a gabled entrance. A one-ken shingled roof is installed at the front. : A palace (shrine) is placed in the inner sanctuary. The palace is a one-bay, hip-and-gabled building with a gabled entrance and horizontal board roof. : There are carvings of celestial maidens on the handrails inside the veranda and a carving of a kirin on the front toad-legs. In the center of the outer sanctuary ceiling is a ink-painted dragon, and the inner sanctuary has a coffered ceiling with brightly colored flowers and birds painted between the coffers. : The Kannon Hall houses a bronze eleven-headed Kannon seated statue with its remains (Nagano Prefecture Treasure) and a wooden standing statue of the eleven-headed Kannon Bodhisattva (Omachi City Tangible Cultural Property). : The Nagano Prefectural Treasure, the bronze eleven-faced seated Kannon statue, is the principal image of the Kannon Hall and is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakuicho. The statue is 19 centimetres tall, and the panel has been removed, leaving only the Buddha body. On the other hand, the wooden standing statue of Eleven-Headed Kannon Bodhisattva is made of cypress wood and inlaid with wood, and parts of it were destroyed by fire. ; Three-story pagoda : It was built in 1711 (8th year of the Hoei era) with the support of Mokishoku Sankyo. It has three bays, three sides and a thatched roof. : On the lower floor, there are seated statues of the Five Wisdom Buddhas (Mahavairocana, Akshobhna, Treasures of Wisdom, Amitabha and Shaka Buddha). : Inside the toad-leg structure on the first floor are carved figures of the twelve Chinese zodiac animals with human bodies and animal faces. ; Other buildings : It houses a worship hall, a shrine office, Gokoku Shrine, and Yasaka Shrine. === Shrine forest === On April 30, 1965, {{Nowrap|17,186.4 [[平方メートル|m2]]}} was designated {{ill|10=ja|11=天然記念物|Natural monument|4=en}} by Nagano Prefecture. {{Cite web|title=若一王子神社社叢|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1615&seq=|access-date=2023-10-21|website=信州の文化財|publisher=八十二文化財団}} [[Chinju no Mori|The shrine grove]] is surrounded by coniferous trees, mainly cedars, but there are also scattered broadleaf trees and one {{ill|7=Hêtre du Japon|10=ja|11=ブナ|Fagus crenata|lt=beech tree|4=en|6=fr}} .{{Clear|right}} == festivals == [[File:若一王子神社由来.jpg|thumb| Origin of Nyakuichioji Shrine (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The festivals are as follows: === festival === * July 17 === annual celebration festival === * Fourth Sunday in July * Yabusame Ritual * Stage Events === Omachi Yabusame === (Source: {{Cite book|title=子ども達による大町流鏑馬|last=|publisher=大町流鏑馬保存会|year=2003|page=9-10|id=|和書}} ) * [[Yabusame|The Yabusame]] of Nyakuichioji Shrine, popularly known as Omachi Yabusame, is said to be one of the three major Yabusame in Japan, along with {{ill|10=ja|11=鶴岡八幡宮|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|4=en}} in Kamakura and [[Shimogamo Shrine|Kamo Shrine]] in Kyoto, and was brought to the area by the Nishina clan, who ruled the area for around 500 years from the Heian period through to the Kamakura period. It is said that this [[Jōkyū|tradition]] began in 829, when [[Emperor Go-Toba]] issues the order to pursue and kill {{ill|10=ja|11=北条義時|Hōjō Yoshitoki|4=en}}, and Nishina Morito offered a yabusame performance before the altar and prayed for good fortune in battle before setting out for battle. Nishina had a deep knowledge of Yabusame at Kamo Shrine, and is said to have brought it to his hometown of Omachi. * Until the Meiji Restoration, it was held jointly with {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科神明宮|Nishina Shinmei Shrine|4=en}} . The same archers performed the event at Nishina Shinmei Shrine on June 16th of the lunar calendar, and at Nyakuichioji Shrine the following day, the 17th, covering a distance of about two ri (approximately 2 ri), but after the Meiji Restoration, they began to hold the event separately. In Omachi, Shigeemon Ito of Kaminakacho proposed selecting archers from among the general parishioners, and donated horse equipment and costumes from his own pocket to each neighborhood, laying the foundation for the Omachi Yabusame, in which ten horsemen from ten neighborhoods compete as they do today. In 1971, it was designated a folk cultural property of Omachi City, and in 2001, it was designated by Nagano Prefecture. ( {{ill|10=ja|11=長野県指定文化財一覧|List of cultural properties designated by Nagano Prefecture|4=en}}) * A distinctive feature of Omachi Yabusame is that the archers are young boys between the ages of six and nine. The boy has makeup on his face, wears hunting clothes and a battle kimono, and is dressed as an archer, carrying a long sword and a Shigefuji bow, with arrows in his quiver. As a child of God possessed by God, I take great care to ensure that my feet do not touch the ground. The archers are called bobo by the locals, and the horses that the bobos ride are accompanied by mouthpieces, fan holders, hat holders, bodyguards, bow carriers, and attendants, all dressed in old-fashioned attire, and the sight of them parading around to the chant of "Hao, hao, hao" gives the performance the appearance of a feudal lord's procession. {{Clear|right}} == Cultural Assets == {{Col-begin}} {{Col-3}} '''Important Cultural Property (重要文化財)''' * Main Shrine (main hall) '''Nagano Prefecture Treasure (Nagano Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Property) (長野県宝（長野県指定有形文化財）)''' * {{ill|Three-Storied Pagoda|ja|三重塔}} * Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon, Remaining Part (十一面観音坐像御正体残闕) {{Col-3}} '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property (長野県指定無形民俗文化財)''' * Yabusame (Archery on horseback) (流鏑馬) '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Natural Monument (長野県指定天然記念物)''' * Shrine Grove (社叢) {{Col-3}} '''Omachi City Designated Tangible Cultural Property (大町市指定有形文化財)''' * Kannon Hall and its Repository (観音堂および厨子) * Standing Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon (十一面観音立像) * Former Portable Shrine of Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社の旧神輿) {{Col-end}} == Traffic access == * Approximately 10 minutes walk from {{ill|10=ja|11=北大町駅|Kita-Ōmachi Station|4=en}} on the [[East Japan Railway Company|JR]] {{ill|10=ja|11=大糸線|Ōito Line|4=en}} == Gallery == the fifth hall of Nachi Taisha, to be the guardian deity of {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科荘|Nishina Manor}} . {{Cite book|title=大町市史|publisher=|editor-last=|volume=|page=255|id=|和書}} Since then, the temple has been called "Nyakuichi no Miya" (Nyakuichioji Temple, Oji Gongen). During this time, Morito gained the favor of [[Emperor Go-Toba]] and served him as {{ill|10=ja|11=西面武士|a Western Guard warrior}} . When the Nishina clan was destroyed along with their lord the {{ill|7=Clan Takeda|10=ja|11=武田氏|Takeda clan|4=en|6=fr}}, the rulers of Japan after [[Oda Nobunaga]] made Azumi County the territory of successive lords of {{ill|10=ja|11=松本城|Matsumoto Castle|4=en}} and came under the protection of the Matsumoto Domain . During [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, when {{ill|10=ja|11=神仏分離|Shinbutsu bunri|lt=Shinto and Buddhism were separated|4=en|6=fr}}, the temple name was abolished and the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1931 ( [[Shōwa period|Showa]] 6), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in 1976 (Showa 51), it was added to the list of beppyo shrines of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Shinto-Buddhist syncretism == The shrine features both torii gates and shrine buildings, as seen in Shinto shrines, and Kannon halls and {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda|lt=three-storied pagodas}}, as seen in Buddhist temples, coexisting within the same precincts, preserving the appearance of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. It is said that the Nyakui Onji Shrine was preserved in this form because, during the Meiji Restoration, in response to the movement to abolish Buddhism initiated by the Matsumoto domain, the predecessors ingeniously built small embankments between each building, arguing that the shrine and the temple were separate entities. {{Cite book|title=若一王子神社昔語り|publisher=|year=2009|editor-last=大町の伝承文化を守る会|id=|和書}} . [[File:若一王子神社鳥居と三重塔.jpg|none|thumb| Torii gate and three-story pagoda of Nyakuiichioji Shrine]] {{Clear|right}} == Temple grounds == [[File:若一王子神社本殿.jpg|thumb|main hall]] [[File:若一王子神社観音堂.jpg|thumb| Kannon Hall (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|thumb| Three-story pagoda (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:若一王子神社のブナ.jpg|thumb| Beech trees growing within the temple grounds (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The main hall was built by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛康|Nishina Moriyasu}} in [[1556]] and is designated as an Important Cultural Property. The worship hall was donated to the temple in [[1975]] as part of the former shrine building of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] . The Kannon Hall to the east of the main hall houses a statue of the {{ill|10=ja|11=十一面観音|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Eleven-Headed Kannon|4=en}}, which is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakui. There is also a {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda}}. === building === The main buildings within the grounds are as follows: ; main hall (Important Cultural Property) : The one-bay shrine is made in the Kasuga style with wooden corners and a cypress bark roof. ; Kannon Hall (Nagano Prefectural Treasure) : Built in 1706 ( [[Hōei|Hoei]] 3). The building is three bays wide, has a hipped roof, thatched roof and a gabled entrance. A one-ken shingled roof is installed at the front. : A palace (shrine) is placed in the inner sanctuary. The palace is a one-bay, hip-and-gabled building with a gabled entrance and horizontal board roof. : There are carvings of celestial maidens on the handrails inside the veranda and a carving of a kirin on the front toad-legs. In the center of the outer sanctuary ceiling is a ink-painted dragon, and the inner sanctuary has a coffered ceiling with brightly colored flowers and birds painted between the coffers. : The Kannon Hall houses a bronze eleven-headed Kannon seated statue with its remains (Nagano Prefecture Treasure) and a wooden standing statue of the eleven-headed Kannon Bodhisattva (Omachi City Tangible Cultural Property). : The Nagano Prefectural Treasure, the bronze eleven-faced seated Kannon statue, is the principal image of the Kannon Hall and is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakuicho. The statue is 19 centimetres tall, and the panel has been removed, leaving only the Buddha body. On the other hand, the wooden standing statue of Eleven-Headed Kannon Bodhisattva is made of cypress wood and inlaid with wood, and parts of it were destroyed by fire. ; Three-story pagoda : It was built in 1711 (8th year of the Hoei era) with the support of Mokishoku Sankyo. It has three bays, three sides and a thatched roof. : On the lower floor, there are seated statues of the Five Wisdom Buddhas (Mahavairocana, Akshobhna, Treasures of Wisdom, Amitabha and Shaka Buddha). : Inside the toad-leg structure on the first floor are carved figures of the twelve Chinese zodiac animals with human bodies and animal faces. ; Other buildings : It houses a worship hall, a shrine office, Gokoku Shrine, and Yasaka Shrine. === Shrine forest === On April 30, 1965, {{Nowrap|17,186.4 [[平方メートル|m2]]}} was designated {{ill|10=ja|11=天然記念物|Natural monument|4=en}} by Nagano Prefecture. {{Cite web|title=若一王子神社社叢|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1615&seq=|access-date=2023-10-21|website=信州の文化財|publisher=八十二文化財団}} [[Chinju no Mori|The shrine grove]] is surrounded by coniferous trees, mainly cedars, but there are also scattered broadleaf trees and one {{ill|7=Hêtre du Japon|10=ja|11=ブナ|Fagus crenata|lt=beech tree|4=en|6=fr}} .{{Clear|right}} == festivals == [[File:若一王子神社由来.jpg|thumb| Origin of Nyakuichioji Shrine (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The festivals are as follows: === festival === * July 17 === annual celebration festival === * Fourth Sunday in July * Yabusame Ritual * Stage Events === Omachi Yabusame === (Source: {{Cite book|title=子ども達による大町流鏑馬|last=|publisher=大町流鏑馬保存会|year=2003|page=9-10|id=|和書}} ) * [[Yabusame|The Yabusame]] of Nyakuichioji Shrine, popularly known as Omachi Yabusame, is said to be one of the three major Yabusame in Japan, along with {{ill|10=ja|11=鶴岡八幡宮|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|4=en}} in Kamakura and [[Shimogamo Shrine|Kamo Shrine]] in Kyoto, and was brought to the area by the Nishina clan, who ruled the area for around 500 years from the Heian period through to the Kamakura period. It is said that this [[Jōkyū|tradition]] began in 829, when [[Emperor Go-Toba]] issues the order to pursue and kill {{ill|10=ja|11=北条義時|Hōjō Yoshitoki|4=en}}, and Nishina Morito offered a yabusame performance before the altar and prayed for good fortune in battle before setting out for battle. Nishina had a deep knowledge of Yabusame at Kamo Shrine, and is said to have brought it to his hometown of Omachi. * Until the Meiji Restoration, it was held jointly with {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科神明宮|Nishina Shinmei Shrine|4=en}} . The same archers performed the event at Nishina Shinmei Shrine on June 16th of the lunar calendar, and at Nyakuichioji Shrine the following day, the 17th, covering a distance of about two ri (approximately 2 ri), but after the Meiji Restoration, they began to hold the event separately. In Omachi, Shigeemon Ito of Kaminakacho proposed selecting archers from among the general parishioners, and donated horse equipment and costumes from his own pocket to each neighborhood, laying the foundation for the Omachi Yabusame, in which ten horsemen from ten neighborhoods compete as they do today. In 1971, it was designated a folk cultural property of Omachi City, and in 2001, it was designated by Nagano Prefecture. ( {{ill|10=ja|11=長野県指定文化財一覧|List of cultural properties designated by Nagano Prefecture|4=en}}) * A distinctive feature of Omachi Yabusame is that the archers are young boys between the ages of six and nine. The boy has makeup on his face, wears hunting clothes and a battle kimono, and is dressed as an archer, carrying a long sword and a Shigefuji bow, with arrows in his quiver. As a child of God possessed by God, I take great care to ensure that my feet do not touch the ground. The archers are called bobo by the locals, and the horses that the bobos ride are accompanied by mouthpieces, fan holders, hat holders, bodyguards, bow carriers, and attendants, all dressed in old-fashioned attire, and the sight of them parading around to the chant of "Hao, hao, hao" gives the performance the appearance of a feudal lord's procession. {{Clear|right}} == Cultural Assets == {{Col-begin}} {{Col-3}} '''Important Cultural Property (重要文化財)''' * Main Shrine (main hall) '''Nagano Prefecture Treasure (Nagano Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Property) (長野県宝（長野県指定有形文化財）)''' * {{ill|Three-Storied Pagoda|ja|三重塔}} * Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon, Remaining Part (十一面観音坐像御正体残闕) {{Col-3}} '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property (長野県指定無形民俗文化財)''' * Yabusame (Archery on horseback) (流鏑馬) '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Natural Monument (長野県指定天然記念物)''' * Shrine Grove (社叢) {{Col-3}} '''Omachi City Designated Tangible Cultural Property (大町市指定有形文化財)''' * Kannon Hall and its Repository (観音堂および厨子) * Standing Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon (十一面観音立像) * Former Portable Shrine of Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社の旧神輿) {{Col-end}} == Traffic access == * Approximately 10 minutes walk from {{ill|10=ja|11=北大町駅|Kita-Ōmachi Station|4=en}} on the [[East Japan Railway Company|JR]] {{ill|10=ja|11=大糸線|Ōito Line|4=en}} == Gallery == {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} – A god enshrined in the fifth shrine {{ill|10=ja|11=熊野那智大社|Kumano Nachi Taisha|en}} * [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Omikami]] * [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * {{ill|10=ja|11=仁品王|King Nishinao}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=妹耶姫|Princess Imoya}} [[ja:若一王子神社]] == history == '''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社}}''' is said to have originated during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], when Prince Nishina, who ruled the area, built a shrine dedicated to [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]], the goddess of water. {{Cite journal|last=三橋建 監修|date=2016-04|title=穂高神社・武水別神社 手長神社・若一王子神社|publisher=[[デアゴスティーニ・ジャパン]]|issue=115|page=14|和書}} The location where it was built was near a waterway called a "seki" (dam) that was developed by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科氏|the Nishina clan|de|Nishina_(Klan)}} during the Kamakura period, and was an important location for diverting water into the city center. {{Cite journal|last=太田勝一|last2=高橋康|title=長野県北西部、仁科山地の地質と斜面崩壊|url=https://www.omachi-sanpaku.com/sanpaku/bull/docs/bulletin8.pdf|journal=市立大町山岳博物館研究紀要|volume=8|pages=1-14|和書}} The temple was founded It has three bays, three sides and a thatched roof. : On the lower floor, there are seated statues of the Five Wisdom Buddhas (Mahavairocana, Akshobhna, Treasures of Wisdom, Amitabha and Shaka Buddha). : Inside the toad-leg structure on the first floor are carved figures of the twelve Chinese zodiac animals with human bodies and animal faces. ; Other buildings : It houses a worship hall, a shrine office, Gokoku Shrine, and Yasaka Shrine. === Shrine forest === On April 30, 1965, {{Nowrap|17,186.4 [[平方メートル|m2]]}} was designated {{ill|10=ja|11=天然記念物|Natural monument|4=en}} by Nagano Prefecture. {{Cite web|title=若一王子神社社叢|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1615&seq=|access-date=2023-10-21|website=信州の文化財|publisher=八十二文化財団}} [[Chinju no Mori|The shrine grove]] is surrounded by coniferous trees, mainly cedars, but there are also scattered broadleaf trees and one {{ill|7=Hêtre du Japon|10=ja|11=ブナ|Fagus crenata|lt=beech tree|4=en|6=fr}} .{{Clear|right}} == festivals == [[File:若一王子神社由来.jpg|thumb| Origin of Nyakuichioji Shrine (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The festivals are as follows: === festival === * July 17 === annual celebration festival === * Fourth Sunday in July * Yabusame Ritual * Stage Events === Omachi Yabusame === (Source: {{Cite book|title=子ども達による大町流鏑馬|last=|publisher=大町流鏑馬保存会|year=2003|page=9-10|id=|和書}} ) * [[Yabusame|The Yabusame]] of Nyakuichioji Shrine, popularly known as Omachi Yabusame, is said to be one of the three major Yabusame in Japan, along with {{ill|10=ja|11=鶴岡八幡宮|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|4=en}} in Kamakura and [[Shimogamo Shrine|Kamo Shrine]] in Kyoto, and was brought to the area by the Nishina clan, who ruled the area for around 500 years from the Heian period through to the Kamakura period. It is said that this [[Jōkyū|tradition]] began in 829, when [[Emperor Go-Toba]] issues the order to pursue and kill {{ill|10=ja|11=北条義時|Hōjō Yoshitoki|4=en}}, and Nishina Morito offered a yabusame performance before the altar and prayed for good fortune in battle before setting out for battle. Nishina had a deep knowledge of Yabusame at Kamo Shrine, and is said to have brought it to his hometown of Omachi. * Until the Meiji Restoration, it was held jointly with {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科神明宮|Nishina Shinmei Shrine|4=en}} . The same archers performed the event at Nishina Shinmei Shrine on June 16th of the lunar calendar, and at Nyakuichioji Shrine the following day, the 17th, covering a distance of about two ri (approximately 2 ri), but after the Meiji Restoration, they began to hold the event separately. In Omachi, Shigeemon Ito of Kaminakacho proposed selecting archers from among the general parishioners, and donated horse equipment and costumes from his own pocket to each neighborhood, laying the foundation for the Omachi Yabusame, in which ten horsemen from ten neighborhoods compete as they do today. In 1971, it was designated a folk cultural property of Omachi City, and in 2001, it was designated by Nagano Prefecture. ( {{ill|10=ja|11=長野県指定文化財一覧|List of cultural properties designated by Nagano Prefecture|4=en}}) * A distinctive feature of Omachi Yabusame is that the archers are young boys between the ages of six and nine. The boy has makeup on his face, wears hunting clothes and a battle kimono, and is dressed as an archer, carrying a long sword and a Shigefuji bow, with arrows in his quiver. As a child of God possessed by God, I take great care to ensure that my feet do not touch the ground. The archers are called bobo by the locals, and the horses that the bobos ride are accompanied by mouthpieces, fan holders, hat holders, bodyguards, bow carriers, and attendants, all dressed in old-fashioned attire, and the sight of them parading around to the chant of "Hao, hao, hao" gives the performance the appearance of a feudal lord's procession. {{Clear|right}} == Cultural Assets == (長野県宝（長野県指定有形文化財）)''' * {{ill|Three-Storied Pagoda|ja|三重塔}} * Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon, Remaining Part (十一面観音坐像御正体残闕) {{Col-3}} '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property (長野県指定無形民俗文化財)''' * Yabusame (Archery on horseback) (流鏑馬) '''Nagano Prefecture Designated Natural Monument (長野県指定天然記念物)''' * Shrine Grove (社叢) {{Col-3}} '''Omachi City Designated Tangible Cultural Property (大町市指定有形文化財)''' * Kannon Hall and its Repository (観音堂および厨子) * Standing Statue of the Eleven-Faced Kannon (十一面観音立像) * Former Portable Shrine of Yasaka Shrine (八坂神社の旧神輿) {{Col-end}} == Traffic access == * Approximately 10 minutes walk from {{ill|10=ja|11=北大町駅|Kita-Ōmachi Station|4=en}} on the [[East Japan Railway Company|JR]] {{ill|10=ja|11=大糸線|Ōito Line|4=en}} == Gallery == 若一王子神社 拝殿
（2018年7月22日撮影）|location=[[長野県]][[大町市]]大字[[大町 (大町市)|大町]]2097|ISO=JP-20|緯度度=36|緯度分=30|緯度秒=56.5|経度度=137|経度分=51|経度秒=12.5|ラベルcoordinates=|map=Japan Nagano|deity={{Ublist| 若一王子 | 天照大神 | 伊弉冉尊 | 仁品王 | 妹耶姫 }}|神体=|rank=県社・別表神社|established=（伝）[[垂仁天皇]]の時代（[[仁科濫觴記]]）|宮司=|main hall=[[春日造]]|alternative name={{Ublist| 若一の宮 | 王子権現 | [[若一王寺]] }}|札所等=|festival=[[7月17日]]|festival=}}'''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社|fr|Nyakuichi-jinja}} (若一王子神社, Nyakuichiōji jinja)''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located in {{ill|10=ja|11=大町_(大町市)|Omachi}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=大町市|Ōmachi, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Ōmachi}}, [[Nagano Prefecture]] . Its former {{ill|10=ja|11=rank|rank}} was that of [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]], but it is currently [[Beppyo shrine|a beppyo shrine]] under [[Association of Shinto Shrines|the Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It worships {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} == Worshipped deities == The following five gods are enshrined here: * {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji|8=fr}} – A god enshrined in the fifth shrine {{ill|10=ja|11=熊野那智大社|Kumano Nachi Taisha|en}} * [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Omikami]] * [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]] * {{ill|10=ja|11=仁品王|King Nishinao}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=妹耶姫|Princess Imoya}} [[ja:若一王子神社]] == history == '''{{ill|Nyakuichiōji Shrine|simple|User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji Shrine|en:Draft|Nyakuichi_Ouji_Shrine|ja|若一王子神社}}''' is said to have originated during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], when Prince Nishina, who ruled the area, built a shrine dedicated to [[Izanami|Izanami-no-Mikoto]], the goddess of water. {{Cite journal|last=三橋建 監修|date=2016-04|title=穂高神社・武水別神社 手長神社・若一王子神社|publisher=[[デアゴスティーニ・ジャパン]]|issue=115|page=14|和書}} The location where it was built was near a waterway called a "seki" (dam) that was developed by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科氏|the Nishina clan|de|Nishina_(Klan)}} during the Kamakura period, and was an important location for diverting water into the city center. {{Cite journal|last=太田勝一|last2=高橋康|title=長野県北西部、仁科山地の地質と斜面崩壊|url=https://www.omachi-sanpaku.com/sanpaku/bull/docs/bulletin8.pdf|journal=市立大町山岳博物館研究紀要|volume=8|pages=1-14|和書}} The temple was founded [[Kamakura period|in the Kamakura period]] when {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛遠|Nishina Morito}}, a local lord who ruled {{ill|10=ja|11=安曇郡|Azumi-gun|lt=the Azumi County}} area, made a pilgrimage to {{Ill|Kumano Gongen|simple|User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen|fr}} in [[Kii Province]] and invited {{ill|Nyakuichiōji|lt=Nyakuichiōji|ja|若一王子|en:draft|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Nyakuichi Ouji}}, who is enshrined in the fifth hall of Nachi Taisha, to be the guardian deity of {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科荘|Nishina Manor}} . {{Cite book|title=大町市史|publisher=|editor-last=|volume=|page=255|id=|和書}} Since then, the temple has been called "Nyakuichi no Miya" (Nyakuichioji Temple, Oji Gongen). During this time, Morito gained the favor of [[Emperor Go-Toba]] and served him as {{ill|10=ja|11=西面武士|a Western Guard warrior}} . When the Nishina clan was destroyed along with their lord the {{ill|7=Clan Takeda|10=ja|11=武田氏|Takeda clan|4=en|6=fr}}, the rulers of Japan after [[Oda Nobunaga]] made Azumi County the territory of successive lords of {{ill|10=ja|11=松本城|Matsumoto Castle|4=en}} and came under the protection of the Matsumoto Domain . During [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] era, when {{ill|10=ja|11=神仏分離|Shinbutsu bunri|lt=Shinto and Buddhism were separated|4=en|6=fr}}, the temple name was abolished and the shrine was renamed to its current name. In 1931 ( [[Shōwa period|Showa]] 6), it was promoted to a prefectural shrine, and in 1976 (Showa 51), it was added to the list of beppyo shrines of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Shinto-Buddhist syncretism == The shrine features both torii gates and shrine buildings, as seen in Shinto shrines, and Kannon halls and {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda|lt=three-storied pagodas}}, as seen in Buddhist temples, coexisting within the same precincts, preserving the appearance of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. It is said that the Nyakui Onji Shrine was preserved in this form because, during the Meiji Restoration, in response to the movement to abolish Buddhism initiated by the Matsumoto domain, the predecessors ingeniously built small embankments between each building, arguing that the shrine and the temple were separate entities. {{Cite book|title=若一王子神社昔語り|publisher=|year=2009|editor-last=大町の伝承文化を守る会|id=|和書}} . [[File:若一王子神社鳥居と三重塔.jpg|none|thumb| Torii gate and three-story pagoda of Nyakuiichioji Shrine]] {{Clear|right}} == Temple grounds == [[File:若一王子神社本殿.jpg|thumb|main hall]] [[File:若一王子神社観音堂.jpg|thumb| Kannon Hall (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:大町市若一王子神社の三重塔.jpg|thumb| Three-story pagoda (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] [[File:若一王子神社のブナ.jpg|thumb| Beech trees growing within the temple grounds (photographed on October 21, 2023)]] The main hall was built by {{ill|10=ja|11=仁科盛康|Nishina Moriyasu}} in [[1556]] and is designated as an Important Cultural Property. The worship hall was donated to the temple in [[1975]] as part of the former shrine building of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] . The Kannon Hall to the east of the main hall houses a statue of the {{ill|10=ja|11=十一面観音|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Eleven-Headed Kannon|4=en}}, which is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakui. There is also a {{ill|10=ja|11=三重塔|three-story pagoda}}. === building === The main buildings within the grounds are as follows: ; main hall (Important Cultural Property) : The one-bay shrine is made in the Kasuga style with wooden corners and a cypress bark roof. ; Kannon Hall (Nagano Prefectural Treasure) : Built in 1706 ( [[Hōei|Hoei]] 3). The building is three bays wide, has a hipped roof, thatched roof and a gabled entrance. A one-ken shingled roof is installed at the front. : A palace (shrine) is placed in the inner sanctuary. The palace is a one-bay, hip-and-gabled building with a gabled entrance and horizontal board roof. : There are carvings of celestial maidens on the handrails inside the veranda and a carving of a kirin on the front toad-legs. In the center of the outer sanctuary ceiling is a ink-painted dragon, and the inner sanctuary has a coffered ceiling with brightly colored flowers and birds painted between the coffers. : The Kannon Hall houses a bronze eleven-headed Kannon seated statue with its remains (Nagano Prefecture Treasure) and a wooden standing statue of the eleven-headed Kannon Bodhisattva (Omachi City Tangible Cultural Property). : The Nagano Prefectural Treasure, the bronze eleven-faced seated Kannon statue, is the principal image of the Kannon Hall and is said to be the local Buddha of Prince Nyakuicho. The statue is 19 centimetres tall, and the panel has been removed, leaving only the Buddha body.
